The bottle must read as compact and rectangular, never tall, narrow, cylindrical, long-necked, perfume-like, syrup-like, supplement-like, or cosmetic. The catalog/display name contains the word Tok, but the physical bottle label does not print TOK anywhere. This structured package truth outranks any stale AI-generated photoshoot or historical reference that shows a taller bottle, a narrower body, different shoulders, a longer neck, or TOK on the label.
MWTCB_25ML_CAP_BURUNG.scale_lock: Bottle stays at exact compact pocket-size traditional herbal-oil scale — a short, flat-bodied glass bottle that is clearly larger and wider than a lip-balm or chapstick roll-on, yet still shorter than an adult palm and about two fingers wide. It fits naturally in a relaxed palm or a secure two-to-three-finger side grip and reads as a small handheld household herbal-oil bottle. Never shrink it toward roll-on, lip-balm, chapstick, or vial proportions, and never enlarge it into a tall perfume, supplement, syrup, spray, cosmetic, or oversized medicine bottle. Never upscale it to dominate the hand, the face, or the frame. Keep the bottle at a natural handheld depth plane and do not place it much closer to the camera lens than the presenter's face or hand.
